study type: Pilot safety trial with historical controls
cohort: 39 maternal-infant dyads undergoing elective cesarean delivery with delayed cord clamping were compared to 112 historical control dyads undergoing elective cesarean delivery with immediate cord clamping.
finding: Delayed cord clamping up to 120 seconds during elective cesarean delivery was associated with decreased maternal blood loss and transfusions, reduced newborn anemia, but increased newborn cold stress/hypothermia.
